name: A stronger open-vocabulary dense extractor for EVERY row of Table I (tab:replica), Replica and ScanNet: three published training-free candidates against the incumbent LSeg, chosen on validation 2D segmentation, then every map re-built and every row re-run once on test
status: DRAFT written 2026-10-24, uncommitted. No candidate has run on any test frame. Before this file existed no candidate ran on any dataset frame; after it was written, a smoke check ran each extractor on 3 VALIDATION frames only (load, shapes, memory, time; docs/reports/2026-10-20-figures-video/logs/extractor_stage1.md), which changed no rule (only the gpu caps below are filled from it). scripts/extractor_select.sh and scripts/extractor_tab1.sh refuse every stage while this file is untracked or modified. The lead fixes the open decisions, sets 'registered', and commits this file and the code before any stage-A run.
registered: 2026-10-24, before any stage A run; lead decisions: Q1 published templates per method, Q2 margin 1.0, Q3 keep all three candidates in stage A, Q4 replace Table I only if C1 holds, Q5 research licences accepted for an academic paper, Q6 keep the existing ProxyCLIP resize convention

pipeline.stage_ab: scripts/extractor_select.sh (stage A: scripts/extractor_2d.py per dataset and extractor; stage B: scripts/extractor_select.py select)
pipeline.stage_c: scripts/extractor_tab1.sh (DATASET=replica|scannet, STAGE=val|test|table, then STAGE=claim once both tables exist)

after: A later attempt, after Table I (v1 and v2), the spatial-smoothing and the view-fusion attempts were final. Every map row of Table I (ours P0/P1/P2, averaging, NormLift, Feature 3DGS, LEGaussians, CSS) lifts the same LSeg features (ViT-L/16, d = 512, PCA to 64), so the rows tie within ~0.4 mIoU; the 2D row applies LSeg per frame. LSeg was chosen on Replica validation on 2026-09-29 (docs/reports/2026-09-29-data-and-baselines/attempts/05-extractor-study.md: worst-scene 2D mIoU, 20 frames per scene) over ClearCLIP (13.4 vs 23.2), dino.txt (23.7 per pixel but 22.7 on the PCA-64 path), Talk2DINO ViT-B (21.7) and ProxyCLIP ViT-B/16 + DINOv2-B (20.3). The candidates below are stronger published configurations not tried then.

radseg.method: RADSeg (Alama et al., CVPR 2026 Findings, arXiv 2511.19704), without the SAM refinement of RADSeg+ (it prompts SAM with the coarse class masks: class-dependent, gives no feature). C-RADIOv3-B backbone with SCRA in its last block, 336/224 windows, SCGA over the frame, the siglip2 adaptor head; text: the SigLIP2 so400m text tower (RADIO's teacher).
radseg.setting: the paper's mid-resolution setting for ADE20K / Pascal Context (Table A.1): short side 576, crop 336, stride 224, SCRA and SCGA scaling 10, fp32 (amp False). 640x480 and 648x484 frames -> 896x672 input -> (42, 56, 1152) tokens.
radseg.published: mid resolution, mean mIoU over Context59, VOC20, COCO-Stuff, ADE20K, Cityscapes: RADSeg base 48.00 vs Trident (ViT-H) 47.02, ProxyCLIP (ViT-H) 43.58, Talk2DINO 43.00 (arXiv 2511.19704v2 Table 1, Table A.2). 3D (RayFronts mapping, feature-space aggregation): Replica 32.29 / ScanNet 36.29 mIoU (Table 2).
radseg.compute: 106M vision parameters; 0.115 s per image on a V100 in fp32 at mid resolution (Table A.3); SigLIP2 text tower 708M parameters (per query, cached)
radseg.code: github.com/RADSeg-OVSS/RADSeg @ 3fe8789 (MIT; read, re-implemented); RADIO model code github.com/NVlabs/RADIO @ 4ffaf15 (NVIDIA Source Code License for RADIO: research / evaluation use only; imported)

proxyclip_h.method: ProxyCLIP (Lan et al., ECCV 2024, arXiv 2408.04883) at its strongest published configuration: OpenCLIP ViT-H/14 (laion2b_s32b_b79k) with the DINO ViT-B/8 proxy (the repo default 'dino').
proxyclip_h.setting: ADE20K config: short side 448 (sides rounded to multiples of 8 so that windows tile the 8-px proxy grid: 640x480 -> 600x448), crop 336, stride 112, beta 1.2, gamma 3.0, fp16 on CUDA. -> (56, 75, 1024) tokens.
proxyclip_h.published: mean mIoU over 8 benchmarks: 44.4 (ViT-H/14) vs 42.3 (ViT-B/16) (arXiv 2408.04883 Table 1); ADE20K 24.2 vs 20.2
proxyclip_h.compute: CLIP ViT-H/14 632M + DINO ViT-B/8 86M; 8 windows per 640x480 frame
proxyclip_h.code: github.com/mc-lan/ProxyCLIP @ a0e38d1 (NTU S-Lab License 1.0: non-commercial use only; read, re-implemented in usplat/extractors/proxyclip.py, which proxyclip_h.py subclasses)

trident.method: Trident (Shi, Dong, Xu, ICCV 2025, arXiv 2411.09219) at its ViT-H/14 setting without the SAM refinement (class-dependent prompts): per-window proxy attention (CLIP ViT-H/14 laion2b_s32b_b79k values, DINO ViT-B/16 proxy), windows spliced on the frame's CLIP grid, then aggregated over the whole frame with the thresholded last-block attention of SAM ViT-H.
trident.setting: ADE20K / Context config: short side 576, crop 336, stride 224, beta 1.2, gamma 3.0, cos_fac 1.2, refine_neg_cos True, fp16 on CUDA. -> (48, 64, 1024) tokens on SAM's valid grid.
trident.published: mean mIoU over 8 benchmarks, ViT-H/14 + SAM-H: 47.1 without refinement (Table 4, 'affinity'), 48.6 with it, ProxyCLIP ViT-H/14 44.4 (arXiv 2411.09219 Tables 2, 4)
trident.compute: 1749M parameters with SAM-H; 15 images/s on an RTX 4090 at 448x448 in fp16, 5.8 GB (Table 8); 1.451 s per image on a V100 fp32 (RADSeg Table A.3)
trident.code: github.com/YuHengsss/Trident @ 7feea10 (Apache-2.0; read, re-implemented); SAM github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything @ dca509f (Apache-2.0; imported)

order_text: tie-break order of stage B, fixed by published compute (cheapest first): RADSeg-B 0.115 s, ProxyCLIP-H, Trident-H 1.451 s per image (V100, RADSeg Table A.3)

not_chosen.dinotxt, talk2dino (ViT-B), proxyclip (V: already compared on Replica validation in attempt 05 and lost to LSeg
not_chosen.NACLIP, SCLIP, ClearCLIP with larger CLI: below ProxyCLIP in the same benchmarks (e.g. SCLIP ViT-H/14 29.1 vs ProxyCLIP 44.4, arXiv 2408.04883 Table 1; NACLIP 38.57 vs RADSeg 48.00, arXiv 2511.19704 Table 1)
not_chosen.RayFronts (NARADIO): superseded by RADSeg from the same group (42.14 vs 48.00, base, Table 1)
not_chosen.dino.txt on DINOv3, TextRegion: DINOv3 weights are gated (licence acceptance needed); TextRegion (47.65 huge) uses SAM2 region masks and ~10x RADSeg's compute
not_chosen.RADSeg+, Trident with SAM refinement, Co: they refine class predictions with the class list (masks, label propagation): no class-agnostic feature to lift
not_chosen.LSeg-like trained segmenters (CAT-Seg, S: they score a given class list, not a text-aligned pixel feature

templates.rule: each method's published template set: the incumbent keeps Table I's 5 LSeg templates; the three candidates use the 80 OpenAI ImageNet templates, which RADSeg, Trident and ProxyCLIP all publish (identical lists). Fixed before any candidate ran on a dataset frame; no template is chosen on our data.
templates.files_text: copies of configs/vocab_replica.json / vocab_scannet.json (sha256 recorded in their derived_from) with only templates_by_extractor extended; classes, prompts, ignore ids and merges unchanged

replica.test_look: a FURTHER look at the Replica test split: earlier looks were Table I v1, the views test (and the room_0 repeat), the Table IV ablations, Table I v2, the qualitative render, the spatial-smoothing attempt and the view-fusion attempt (fusion/replica/look_test.json)

scannet.test_look: the FOURTH look at the ScanNet test split: Table I v1 + v2 (scannet_tab1/look_test.json), the spatial-smoothing attempt (smooth/scannet/look_test.json), the view-fusion attempt (fusion/scannet/look_test.json), then this

stage_a.what: per extractor (incumbent + 3 candidates) and dataset: the 2D segmentation of every validation evaluation frame (Replica office_0, room_2: Sequence_2 every 10th frame, 90 each; ScanNet scene0000_00, scene0062_00: frames 5, 25, 45, ..., 279 and 37) through Table I's 2D-row path (scripts/extractor_2d.py): tokens -> bilinear upsample to the label grid (downscale 2) -> unit -> PCA-64 fit like run_mapping.py on the first 20 mapping frames of the scene (seed 0) -> logits with the PCA-projected text of the present classes (decode first, F7) -> argmax over every labelled pixel
stage_a.metric: per scene mIoU over the classes present in its evaluation frames (usplat.seg_eval.confusion_iou; Table I's variant 'all'); A_D(x) = mean over dataset D's two validation scenes (Table I reports means over scenes)
stage_a.secondary: pixel accuracy and the full-dimensional (no PCA) 2D mIoU: reported, never used by a rule

reproduction.text: R0, independent check before any decision: the incumbent's per-scene PCA-64 2D mIoU must equal Table I's validation record (datasets.<d>.table1.val, row 2d_features, variant all) within 0.1 points on all four scenes (same frames, same PCA procedure and seed, same text cache). If not, stage A measures something else than Table I: the attempt stops and the gap goes to the lead.

stage_a.text_cache: the incumbent: a COPY of Table I's cache (datasets.<d>.table1.text_cache) in OUT; candidates: a new cache in OUT (eval_seg's key format, so stage C reuses a copy of it)

stage_b.rule: delta_D(x) = A_D(x) - A_D(lseg) for D in {replica, scannet}. Winner = the candidate with the largest min(delta_replica, delta_scannet); candidates within tie_tol of the largest tie and the earliest in 'order' wins.
stage_b.gate: stage C runs only if R0 passed AND the winner's min(delta_replica, delta_scannet) >= margin (1.0 mIoU point on BOTH datasets). Otherwise the attempt ends on validation: LSeg stays in every row, the stage A table is reported (appendix / report), and no test scene is touched.
stage_b.why_per_dataset: Table I and the paper's claims are per dataset, so the new extractor must help on each. A pooled pixel mean would be dominated by ScanNet (scene0000_00 alone holds 18.6M of the 33.5M validation pixels) and could hide a loss on Replica; scene means keep each validation scene equally weighted, as Table I's means do.
stage_b.why_margin: Table I's rows already tie within 0.4 mIoU on the same features, attempt 05 treated a 0.5-point 2D difference (dino.txt vs LSeg) as noise, and two validation scenes per dataset carry large between-scene spread (Table I validation 2D mIoU: Replica 29.6 / 31.9, ScanNet 57.0 / 78.1). A re-mapping of 18 scenes is justified only by a clear 2D gain on both datasets.

stage_c.what: with the winner W only: re-map every Replica (8) and ScanNet (10) scene on the EXISTING 3DGS maps (datasets.<d>.maps, never refitted), with run_mapping.py exactly as Table I (Replica: Sequence_1 stride 5, CSS frames Sequence_2 stride 10; ScanNet: prepared scan stride 10, CSS frames eval_s20o5 stride 1; --baselines --feat-dim 64 --pca-frames 20 --seed 0 --downscale 2) except --extractor W and --vocab datasets.<d>.eval.vocab; fields in datasets.<d>.fields (never a Table I field path); distillation exactly as Table I (validation: f3dgs and LEGaussians for every lambda_u of usplat.distill.LEGS_LAMBDAS; test: f3dgs and the lambda_u chosen on validation); eval_seg.py exactly as Table I (--with-2d, --row-factory usplat.baselines:row_factory,usplat.distill:row_factory, tau_cov 0.5, downscale 2; no --v2-rows: Table I keeps P2) on scene files derived from configs/<d>_{val,test}.json with only the field paths changed
stage_c.rows: every row of Table I: 2D features per frame, averaging, NormLift (1 - R and 1 - C_inter AUSE), Feature 3DGS, LEGaussians (lambda_u chosen on validation), ours P0 / P1 / P2 (+ the P3 rows Table I evaluates), CSS (alpha0 chosen on validation)
stage_c.refit: temperatures (one beta per row; P2's parameters), CSS alpha0, the P3 temperature and LEGaussians' lambda_u are refit on the validation scenes exactly as for Table I (eval_seg --val-scenes; scripts/make_tables.py choose); nothing is carried over from the LSeg run
stage_c.consistency: independent check before the test: the winner's 2D row in the stage C validation evaluation must equal its stage-A record per scene within 0.1 points (same frames, PCA procedure, text); otherwise check-test refuses and the lead decides
stage_c.test_once: the test split of each dataset is evaluated once, with the validation choices, at the validation commit (scripts/ usplat/ configs/ unchanged); every attempt is appended to OUT/look_test.json before it runs; a finished test record is never rerun

claim.headline: miou
claim.C1: The paper may write that the stronger extractor improves our map on dataset D only if, on the test scenes of D, ours P2 with W has a higher mean mIoU (P2 shares P0's labels) than ours P2 in Table I with LSeg AND is higher in at least min_wins[D] test scenes (>= 4/6 Replica, >= 5/8 ScanNet; a tie is not a win). The same rule is computed and reported for Acc, ECE, NLL, Brier and AURC (descriptive unless it holds).
claim.C1_text_if_not: 'with W, ours reaches X vs Y mIoU (better in k of N scenes)': numbers only, no claim of improvement
claim.vs_averaging: the standing of ours against averaging (and every other row) with W is reported as it is (means, scenes better x/N): no claim is pre-registered and none may be added after the test
claim.every_row: every row of the new table is reported (test, mean +- std over scenes, N), with the validation choices, next to Table I's LSeg numbers

disclosure: Paper sentence (Setup or the Table I paragraph): 'After Table I was final we replaced LSeg by <W> in every row; <W> was chosen among three published training-free extractors by a rule registered before any of them ran on our data (configs/extractor_prereg.json: per-frame 2D mIoU on the validation scenes, at least 1 point better than LSeg on both datasets); all maps were rebuilt, every temperature and choice was refit on validation, and the test scenes were evaluated once. This is a later attempt and a further look at the test scenes (Replica: after Table I and six other looks; ScanNet: the fourth).' If the gate fails: 'A stronger extractor, chosen by a registered rule, did not beat LSeg on the validation scenes of both datasets (<numbers>); Table I keeps LSeg.'

gpu.basis: Smoke check 2026-10-24 (3 Replica office_0 validation frames per extractor, scripts/extractor_2d.py smoke mode, RTX 4070 Ti, records in /home/thanhnc/gauss_ws/data/uags_results/extractor/smoke/): peak allocated LSeg 1876 MiB, RADSeg 3838 (incl. the fp32 SigLIP2 text tower, 2.8 GB), ProxyCLIP-H 3985, Trident 4896; extraction 70 / 70 / 281 / 353 ms per frame after warm-up. Stage A cap = peak + ~1.6 GB (more text classes, the PCA). Stage C keeps Table I's caps: mapping 9000 (Table I peak 4.8-5.7 GB in the mapping phase; the extractor phase, <= 4.9 GB, does not overlap it), distillation 7000 and evaluation 7000 (Table I evaluation peaks 2.3-3.7 GB; the 2D row's extractor leaves the GPU before the rows are frozen), all >= the new extractor's peak + 2 GB.

open_decisions: Q1 templates: each method's published set (80 ImageNet templates for the candidates, LSeg keeps its 5) as drafted, or the 5 LSeg templates for every extractor (same text input, but not the candidates' published recipe)
Q2 margin: 1.0 mIoU point on both datasets as drafted, or 0 (any gain), or 0.5
Q3 candidates: all three as drafted, or drop Trident (1.75B parameters, ~10x RADSeg's time; its published gain over ProxyCLIP-H is the SAM affinity) to save GPU time

Q4 what C1 changes: if C1 holds on both datasets, the new table replaces Table I and the LSeg table moves to the appendix; if it holds on one or none, Table I stays and the new table goes to the appendix (drafted). Alternative: always appendix
Q5 licences: RADIO code (NVIDIA Source Code License, research / evaluation only) and ProxyCLIP code (NTU S-Lab, non-commercial) restrict use to research; acceptable for the paper?

Q6 ProxyCLIP-H geometry: its tokens equal the official code's (cos >= 0.9999996 per crop), but like usplat/extractors/proxyclip.py it rounds the resized frame to the 8-px proxy grid (640x480 -> 600x448 instead of 597x448) and averages window tokens instead of per-pixel window logits: 95.9% pixel argmax agreement with the official code on a 640x480 demo frame, 99.67% on a 672x448 frame that needs no rounding. Keep as drafted (the convention of the extractor already compared in attempt 05), or drop ProxyCLIP-H
